title: Queen Vashti Refuses the King's Summons
image_prompt: Women's palace banquet hall: Queen Vashti, seated with dignity among royal women, calmly refusing the command of the king's seven chamberlains to present herself before the men's banquet.

image_prompt: Persian council chamber: Memucan and royal counselors advising King Ahasuerus, while scribes copy sealed imperial letters to be dispatched across the 127 provinces of the empire.

image_prompt: Garden courtyard of the women's palace: young modest Esther listening respectfully to royal keeper Hegai, while cousin Mordecai walks daily before the outer court to inquire after her well-being.

image_prompt: Throne hall of Susa: King Ahasuerus setting the royal golden crown upon Queen Esther's head, surrounded by court nobles during a grand holiday feast in her honor.

title: Mordecai Uncovers the Treasonous Plot
image_prompt: King's stone gate: Mordecai sitting attentively by the entrance, overhearing two conspirators whispering, before reporting the plot to Queen Esther who informs the king in Mordecai's name.

title: Mordecai Refuses to Bow to Haman
image_prompt: Palace entrance: proud Prime Minister Haman passing in rich robes as royal servants bow to the ground, while solitary Mordecai the Jew stands upright in quiet spiritual conviction.

image_prompt: Council chamber: Haman casting lots (Pur) on a carved stone table, then bowing before King Ahasuerus who hands him the royal golden signet ring to seal the edict.

title: The Threatening Decree Dispatched
image_prompt: Courtyard of Susa: royal scribes writing Haman's decree on parchment, dispatching mounted couriers on swift royal horses carrying sealed scrolls, as the city of Susa is thrown into confusion.

title: Mordecai and the People Mourn in Sackcloth
image_prompt: Public square outside the king's gate: Mordecai crying aloud in sackcloth and ashes, handing a copy of the written decree to Queen Esther's chamberlain Hathach.

title: For Such a Time as This
image_prompt: Private palace apartment: chamberlain Hathach delivering Mordecai's piercing challenge to Queen Esther: 'Who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?'

title: Esther Calls for a Three-Day Fast
image_prompt: Esther's chamber: Queen Esther and her maidens kneeling in solemn three-day fasting and prayer, resolved to approach the king with the words: 'If I perish, I perish.'

title: The Golden Sceptre Extended
image_prompt: Throne room of Susa: Queen Esther standing in royal robes in the inner court; King Ahasuerus extends his golden sceptre to her, and she steps forward to touch its top with reverent grace.

title: Haman Boasts to Zeresh and His Friends
image_prompt: Haman's lavish courtyard: proud Haman boasting of his riches and banquet invitation to his wife Zeresh, while planning a high wooden gallows for Mordecai under evening torchlight.

title: The King's Sleepless Night and the Chronicles
image_prompt: Royal bedchamber at midnight: King Ahasuerus awake on his couch, listening as an attendant reads from the book of the chronicles describing how Mordecai saved the king's life.

title: Haman Leads Mordecai in Honor
image_prompt: City streets of Susa: shocked Haman leading the king's royal horse carrying Mordecai dressed in the king's royal robes and crown, proclaiming: 'Thus shall it be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour!'

title: Zeresh Warns Haman
image_prompt: Haman's home: Haman mourning with head covered as his wife Zeresh warns him of his impending fall, just as royal chamberlains arrive to escort him to Esther's banquet.

title: Esther Exposes the Adversary
image_prompt: Royal banquet table: Queen Esther pointing with righteous courage across the table, declaring: 'The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman!', as Haman trembles in terror before the furious king.

title: The Downfall of Haman
image_prompt: Banquet chamber: King Ahasuerus returning from the palace garden in wrath, ordering royal guards to cover Haman's face and lead him away to the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.

title: Mordecai Receives the Royal Signet Ring
image_prompt: Throne room: King Ahasuerus handing his golden signet ring to Mordecai, while Queen Esther looks on with grateful joy, authorized to write a decree for the protection of her people.

title: The Counter-Decree of Defense Dispatched
image_prompt: Scribes' hall in Susa: royal scribes writing Mordecai's decree granting the Jews the right to unite and defend their lives, dispatching couriers on royal dromedaries and swift horses.

title: Mordecai in Royal Apparel and the City Rejoices
image_prompt: City of Susa: Mordecai stepping into the public square clothed in royal blue and white garments with a great crown of gold, as Jewish families celebrate with light, gladness, joy, and honor.

title: The Day of Deliverance and Defense
image_prompt: Thirteenth day of Adar: Jewish communities standing united and resolute under the protection of royal officials across provincial towns, turning a day of danger into triumphant deliverance.

title: The Report to the King and Esther's Petition
image_prompt: Throne room: King Ahasuerus and Queen Esther reviewing the official provincial defense report, with Esther making a formal petition for continued peace and justice in Susa.

title: Rest, Gladness, and Sending Portions
image_prompt: Provincial towns on the fourteenth of Adar: Jewish families celebrating peaceful survival at shared tables, sending gifts of cakes, fruits, and wine portions to one another with radiant smiles.

title: Mordecai Establishes the Feast of Purim
image_prompt: Mordecai's study: Mordecai sealing letters sent to all provinces establishing the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar as the perpetual annual Feast of Purim, celebrating days turned from sorrow to joy.

title: Queen Esther Confirms the Purim Letters
image_prompt: Royal chamber: Queen Esther in royal mantle writing with authority alongside Mordecai, confirming the second letter of Purim with fasts, prayers, and rejoicing for all generations.

title: Mordecai's Greatness and Lasting Peace
image_prompt: Grand Persian court: Mordecai, second in power to King Ahasuerus, surrounded by visiting provincial elders and scribes, seeking the wealth of his people and speaking peace to all his seed.
